summary: Run synchronous store work on its existing blocking handler instead of waiting for a second pool slot

replay.detail: No replay, recovery or derived-data rebuild is introduced.

schema.detail: No database, index, trigger or persisted format changes.

rules.detail: Admission, authority, checkpoint and retention rules are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: List/filter/get, API response and mutation acknowledgement shapes are unchanged. A multi-thread runtime executes nested synchronous work on the already-blocking handler, outside its block_on context. Read budgets and reader leases remain in use; current-thread runtimes retain the spawned path. Writes still wait for committed results and are not made cancellable. Existing profiling gains blocking/queue and blocking/work wall spans.

downtime.detail: Only the normal binary restart is needed; no extra migration or startup phase. Production latency and restart timing remain unmeasured for this change.

manual.detail: No configuration change, data repair or coordinated upgrade is required.

recovery.detail: The execution marker is thread-local and resets after each handler, including unwind. Binary swap-back uses the unchanged store.
